h: Escape tips and cathedral city extras
p: Here's a little secret about escape rooms: the people who do best aren't the ones with the biggest brains, they're the ones who talk the most. As soon as the door shuts, spread out and search everything. Shout out what you find, put it all in one place and start matching things up. If you're stuck on one puzzle, switch to another. It's amazing how often solving something else unlocks the bit that had you stumped.

With the cathedral right outside and so much history in the surrounding streets, an escape game makes a cracking change of pace on a sightseeing day. Families with older children often find it the bit of the trip the kids remember most. Book ahead for Saturdays and school holidays, and get there a few minutes early so you can settle in before the clock starts ticking.

Worcester has a surprising amount to explore beyond the cathedral. The Museum of Royal Worcester, near the cathedral, celebrates the city's famous porcelain-making history with gorgeous collections. Along Friar Street, Greyfriars, a timber-framed merchant's house run by the National Trust, offers a peek into Tudor life, while the Tudor House Museum nearby tells more stories of the city's past. Cricket fans can catch a match at New Road, the picturesque home of Worcestershire County Cricket Club beside the River Severn. The Hive, the city's modern library and archive building with its distinctive golden roof, is worth a look for its architecture alone. And if you want some fresh air, the Malvern Hills are a short drive west, with glorious ridge walks and views across several counties.
